/-!
# Conjecture 9.52

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?

The notebook adds the note that there is an algorithm to decide conjugacy to a given element of
the group. This records a known fact and is not part of the question.

Here "rank" is the Prüfer rank (Mal'cev's special rank): a group has finite rank if there is an
$r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by at most $r$ elements.
The conjugacy problem for a finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ is
soluble if there is an algorithm which decides, for any two words $u, v$ in the letters
$x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$, whether the elements of the group represented by $u$ and $v$
are conjugate. Solubility of the conjugacy problem does not depend on the choice of finite
presentation of the group, so the question is stated for every finite presentation.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's Group.rank (minimum number of generators of a finitely generated group), which is used inside the definition; it is only defined for f.g. groups and does not itself express bounded rank over all f.g. subgroups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.52».HasFinitePruferRank
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of Prüfer (Mal'cev special) rank of a group; 'finite rank' in the statement means there is r such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated by ≤ r elements. Defined as ∃ r, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r.

blocks.name: HasFinitePruferRank
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ has finite (Prüfer) rank if there is an $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFinitePruferRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

blocks.docstring:
The conjugacy problem for the presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is
soluble if the set of pairs of words $(u, v)$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ such that $u$ and $v$
represent conjugate elements of the presented group is decidable. A word is a list of letters
`(i, b) : Fin n × Bool`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)` for $x_i^{-1}$,
as in `FreeGroup.mk`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's ComputablePred (used), IsConj (used), PresentedGroup / FreeGroup.mk (used); no existing predicate packages them as a decision problem.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.52».HasSolubleConjugacyProblem
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib defines the (uniform) conjugacy problem of a finitely presented group. Defined as ComputablePred on pairs of words List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool), asking whether the images under PresentedGroup.mk rels ∘ FreeGroup.mk are conjugate (IsConj).

blocks.name: HasSolubleConjugacyProblem
blocks.text:
/-- The conjugacy problem for the presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is
soluble if the set of pairs of words $(u, v)$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ such that $u$ and $v$
represent conjugate elements of the presented group is decidable. A word is a list of letters
`(i, b) : Fin n × Bool`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)` for $x_i^{-1}$,
as in `FreeGroup.mk`. -/
def HasSolubleConjugacyProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
    IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.2))

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFinitePruferRank_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    HasFinitePruferRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite G
  calc Group.rank H ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset H).card := Group.rank_le (by simp)
    _ ≤ Nat.card G := by
      rw [Finset.card_univ, ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
      exact Nat.card_le_card_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question quantified over all finitely presented soluble groups of finite (Prüfer/Mal'cev) rank; 'soluble conjugacy problem' means the uniform conjugacy problem (decidability of the set of pairs of words that are conjugate, for a fixed finite presentation) is decidable, and the trailing 'Note' sentence merely records the known fact that conjugacy to any single fixed element is decidable, so it poses no separate question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are faithful and structurally equivalent (quantify over all finite presentations ⟨Fin n | rels⟩, Mathlib `IsSolvable`, bespoke finite Prüfer rank, uniform conjugacy problem as `ComputablePred`/`Computable₂` on pairs of raw words via `FreeGroup.mk`, `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ …`). c05 chosen for style: it reuses Mathlib's `Group.rank` for Prüfer rank, includes API tests for both bespoke definitions (its Fin 0 test covers all relator sets, unlike c01's ∅-only test), tags `AMS 3 20` (decidability + group theory, matching the repo's other decidability problem), documents the word convention correctly per `FreeGroup.mk`, and records the trailing Note in the module docstring without formalizing it. Used essentially verbatim; compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.52

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?

The notebook adds the note that there is an algorithm to decide conjugacy to a given element of
the group. This records a known fact and is not part of the question.

$x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$, whether the elements of the group represented by $u$ and $v$
are conjugate. Solubility of the conjugacy problem does not depend on the choice of finite
presentation of the group, so the question is stated for every finite presentation.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.52»

/-- A group $G$ has finite (Prüfer) rank if there is an $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every
finitely generated subgroup of $G$ can be generated by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFinitePruferRank (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

/-- The conjugacy problem for the presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is
soluble if the set of pairs of words $(u, v)$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ such that $u$ and $v$
represent conjugate elements of the presented group is decidable. A word is a list of letters
`(i, b) : Fin n × Bool`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)` for $x_i^{-1}$,
as in `FreeGroup.mk`. -/
def HasSolubleConjugacyProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ComputablePred fun p : List (Fin n × Bool) × List (Fin n × Bool) =>
    IsConj (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.1)) (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk p.2))

/--
Does a finitely presented soluble group of finite rank have soluble conjugacy problem?

A finitely presented group is given as `PresentedGroup rels` with finitely many generators
`Fin n` and a finite set of relators `rels`. "Finite rank" means finite Prüfer rank.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.52» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) →
      HasFinitePruferRank (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) →
      HasSolubleConjugacyProblem (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) := by
  sorry

/-- Every finite group has finite Prüfer rank. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFinitePruferRank_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    HasFinitePruferRank G := by
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite G
  calc Group.rank H ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset H).card := Group.rank_le (by simp)
    _ ≤ Nat.card G := by
      rw [Finset.card_univ, ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
      exact Nat.card_le_card_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective

/-- Any presentation with no generators has soluble conjugacy problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem hasSolubleConjugacyProblem_of_fin_zero (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin 0))) :
    HasSolubleConjugacyProblem rels := by
  refine ⟨fun p => .isTrue ?_, Computable.const true⟩
  obtain ⟨u, v⟩ := p
  obtain rfl : u = v := Subsingleton.elim u v
  exact IsConj.refl _

end Kourovka.«9.52»

items: 'Rank' is read as Prüfer rank (Mal'cev special rank), following the decomposition notes and Robinson's usage in his work on soluble groups of finite rank. Other ranks (torsion-free/Hirsch rank, abelian section rank) were not used.

The question is quantified over all finite presentations ⟨Fin n | rels⟩ with rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)), rather than over abstract groups with an existential finite presentation. Solubility, finite Prüfer rank and decidability of the conjugacy problem are all invariant under isomorphism / change of finite presentation, so this is equivalent to the statement about finitely presented groups.

The conjugacy problem is formalized as computability (ComputablePred) of the set of pairs of words in the generators and their inverses (List (Fin n × Bool), via FreeGroup.mk) that represent conjugate elements. This uses Mathlib's Primcodable encoding of lists and pairs, which is computable, so the notion matches the classical one.
The set of relators is only required to be finite (Finset), not given by any explicit computable data; for a finite set this is the standard reading of a 'finite presentation'.

The notebook's trailing Note (conjugacy to a fixed element is decidable) is recorded in the module docstring as a known fact and not formalized as a separate statement, as the decomposition table prescribes.
answer(True) corresponds to the answer 'yes'. The case n = 0 (trivial group) satisfies the hypotheses and the conclusion (proved as a test), so the hypotheses are not vacuous.

Two category-test theorems with short proofs (finite groups have finite Prüfer rank; presentations with no generators have soluble conjugacy problem) are included as basic API for the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

reviewer_notes: Modeling choices shared by all candidates and adopted in the final file: (1) 'finite rank' = finite Prüfer (Mal'cev special) rank, as fixed by the decomposition notes and Robinson's usage; for finitely generated soluble groups this agrees with finite abelian section rank / minimax, but not with torsion-free (Hirsch) rank, which was deliberately not used. (2) 'Finitely presented group' is modeled by quantifying over all finite presentations with generators Fin n and a Finset of relators; every finitely presented group is isomorphic to one of these and solubility, Prüfer rank and decidability of the conjugacy problem are invariant under isomorphism/change of finite presentation, so this is equivalent to quantifying over abstract groups. (3) 'Soluble conjugacy problem' = uniform conjugacy problem: Mathlib `ComputablePred` (genuinely computable indicator, not a mere classical Decidable instance) on pairs of words List (Fin n × Bool) whose images in the presented group are IsConj; the algorithm may depend on the fixed presentation. (4) The trailing Note (decidability of conjugacy to a fixed element) is a known fact, recorded only in the docstring, per the decomposition table. Boundary check: n = 0 (trivial group) satisfies hypotheses and conclusion (proved as a test), and ℤ is a nontrivial member of the class, so the statement is not vacuous and answer(True)/answer(False) correspond to yes/no. Minor observations on other candidates: c04's docstring/`wordValue` inverts Mathlib's FreeGroup.mk sign convention (self-consistent, not unfaithful); c02/c03/c04/c07/c08 tag only AMS 20; c07 lacks a test for its conjugacy-problem definition. No candidate omitted the slot and no objections to the decomposition were raised.
